clue.text: Relief to have paler option with mortar

indicators.note: an option is an alternative version, so the letters of the word paler are given another arrangement

parts.note: mortar is a building cement binding bricks

explanation.surface: A builder weighs up a paler alternative mixed with mortar to repair a carved relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'option' signals REPLA, a rearrangement of PALER, which then takes CEMENT. 'Relief' looks like a sculpture, but it means a stand-in who takes over a shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief is a substitute worker who takes over from someone, i.e. a stand-in.

clue.text: English retreat, place of great happiness

parts.note: a den is a private room one retreats to

explanation.surface: An English hideaway described as a blissful spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden of paradise is the byword for a state of perfect bliss.

clue.text: National emblem of general and king

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the American Confederate general
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A country's symbol linked to a military commander and a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The national emblem is Wales's vegetable symbol, worn on St David's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is the traditional symbol of Wales, an example of a national badge.

parts.note: to cut someone is to injure them
lass is a word for a girl, especially in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: Someone hurts a young woman with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A short curved blade used by sailors and pirates is a type of sword.

parts.note: an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: A man who is the best at a flamboyant sports club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a society, but here it is a heavy staff, the ceremonial kind carried before officials.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial staff carried before a mayor or in Parliament is an ornate kind of club or cudgel.

clue.text: Sewers off the Isle of Wight?

definitions.meaning: things that sew, i.e. pointed tools with an eye for thread
a row of chalk stacks standing in the sea off the western tip of the Isle of Wight, an English island

explanation.definitionFit: Sewing tools are things that sew, and a famous rock formation off the Isle of Wight shares the same name.

definitions.meaning: the component in a petrol engine that sends current to each spark plug in turn
a wholesaler who hands goods out to shops

explanation.definitionFit: Both the ignition component that shares out sparks and a wholesale dealer share out something to many destinations.

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of Saint George turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: England's patron saint unexpectedly introduces racial separation.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was the South African policy of separating people by race, a form of enforced separation.

definitions.meaning: as in toeing the party ..., an official stance
a boundary, as in drawing the ...

explanation.definitionFit: A party's official stance and a boundary mark are both senses of the same short word.

clue.text: Secret place, it turns out, for containers

indicators.note: it turns out suggests the letters of secret place, turned about, come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A hidden spot proves to be where the storage boxes are.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessels or holders that hold things are containers, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Commotion makes one run on street

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so one and run follow street

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A fuss arises when a person dashes along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or disturbance is a commotion, as in causing a stir.

parts.note: grave means solemn or grim-faced
digger is slang for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.surface: A stern-looking Australian who looks after a church.
explanation.walkthrough: A sexton's traditional duties include digging graves, hence the question mark on a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer whose duties traditionally include digging burial plots.

indicators.note: music can be transposed into another key; here the letters of German score are transposed into a new order

explanation.surface: A German's musical score for the Doris Day film is moved to a new key.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the musical Calamity Jane; read literally, the name describes someone who forecasts calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: A Calamity Jane is a doom-monger who always predicts disaster, an alarmist.

clue.text: Withdrawn, in respect of clues gone wrong

parts.note: re means concerning or in respect of

indicators.note: gone wrong suggests the letters of clues have been put in a faulty order

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from a crossword after the clues go awry.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means solitary or shut away from others, i.e. withdrawn.

clue.text: Story comes up about Conservative leader, with striking effect

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reversed story goes round the leader
in a down clue, comes up means the word for story is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A news item emerges concerning the Tory leader, making a big impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns TALE into ELAT, and 'about' puts the C from 'Conservative leader' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant success or dazzling show is a striking effect.

definitions.meaning: one of the senses, as touch
emotional responsiveness, as in hurting someone's emotions

explanation.definitionFit: Touch is a physical sense and emotional responsiveness is sensibility; the one word covers both.

clue.text: Dowdy woman puts bottom fellow first

indicators.note: first means the abbreviation for fellow goes ahead of the bottom

parts.note: the rump is the backside or bottom

explanation.surface: A drab woman places her lowest-ranked man at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A frumpy woman is one dressed in a drab, old-fashioned way.

clue.text: Second vehicles often show such marks

parts.note: cars are vehicles

explanation.surface: Used cars often bear dents and scratches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second vehicles' reads as second-hand cars, which do often show marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks left on skin after a wound heals, and dents on bodywork, are blemishes.

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the Royal Order of Victoria and Albert
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A passenger switches trains to the Victoria Tube line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Victoria line is a London Underground route, but here it splits into two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To vary is to alter or make different, i.e. change.

clue.text: Grape-juice, something you should not miss

definitions.meaning: unfermented juice pressed from grapes for winemaking

explanation.definitionFit: Freshly pressed juice before fermentation, and an essential item, share the same word.

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts

explanation.surface: People hold out their hands to give a coin to good causes.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm is the inner surface of the hand, used here for the hands themselves.

clue.text: This fish produces pain, and endless harm when excited

indicators.note: when excited suggests the letters are stirred into a new order
endless means the word harm loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A dangerous fish causes pain and harm whenever it is stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the M of HARM to leave HAR, and 'when excited' rearranges PAIN with HAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharp-toothed South American freshwater predator is a kind of fish.

parts.note: normally money obtained dishonestly; read literally, money received when you are unwell

explanation.definitionFit: Wages paid to an employee off work through illness are literally money got while ill.

indicators.note: can make suggests the letters of me tired can be formed into something new

explanation.surface: A shortcoming can leave someone exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: A black mark or flaw counting against someone is a fault.

clue.text: High player in polo takes in tiny volume of water

indicators.note: takes in means the word polo swallows the volume

parts.note: one cc, a cubic centimetre, written I CC, is a tiny volume of water

explanation.surface: A tall water-polo player gulps down a mouthful of the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests water polo; the definition 'High player' is an instrument with a high pitch, not a tall sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: This small flute plays an octave above the ordinary one, so it is a high-pitched instrument.

definitions.meaning: a band of workers or roughs
the Scots verb meaning to go or walk

explanation.definitionFit: A group of workers is a crew, and in Scots dialect the same word is the verb to go.

definitions.meaning: a lake or pond, as in Windermere

explanation.definitionFit: Pure and nothing more is one sense; a lake or pond is the other.

clue.text: Part of the sporran that is odd?

indicators.note: part of means only a section of the word sporran is used

explanation.surface: A section of a Highland pouch is said to be strange.
explanation.walkthrough: A sporran is the pouch worn in front of a Scottish kilt, fitting the Scots word in it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means odd or spare, as of an unmatched item.

clue.text: Facial twitch from ring, relating to ear

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
a tic is an involuntary twitch, often of the face

explanation.surface: A face twitches because of a ringing noise in the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical adjective means of or concerning the organ of hearing.

indicators.note: before means the word for angry is placed ahead of the rearranged tea

parts.note: in temper means angry

indicators.note: break suggests the letters of tea are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A spendthrift loses their temper ahead of a pause for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' turns TEA into ATE; the surface's tea-break is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasteful and lacking self-restraint, a prodigal person is immoderate.

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A trough for animals on a sheep pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: A sheep-run is a grazing pasture, but here it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug or pitcher for water is a vessel, here a drinking one.

parts.note: a shooting brake is an old estate car; read literally, a device that stops a gun from shooting

explanation.definitionFit: The locking lever on a gun prevents it firing, literally a brake on shooting.
